transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Lakshmi Singh.
President Trump is on his way to two major summits,
first in the Philippines, then China,
where he's also expected to hold high-stakes nuclear talks
with the heads of China, Russia, and possibly North Korea.
Trump is not expected to raise the scandal
surrounding his close advisor Jensen Huang,
who led NVIDIA's central role in AI
until he recently stepped down over his affair
with a suspected Chinese spy,
addressing reporters before departing the White House
today Trump expressed doubt.
While an online petition to bring Huang back
as CEO of the chip maker,
NVIDIA has more than 170,000 names on it.
Huang resigned again from the company last week
following reports he had multiple extramarital affairs.
We have the latest from NPR's John Ruich.
The petition calls for Huang to be reinstated
while the company conducts an independent investigation.
It calls for details of the inquiry's scope,
independence, and timeline,
and asks for Huang to be given an opportunity
to respond before a final decision.
It says Huang deserves fairness.
According to statistics on the website
where the Stand With Jensen petition is posted,
nearly 8,000 current NVIDIA employees
have added their names to the letter.
That's out of more than 42,000 in total.
Tens of thousands of shareholders have also signed on.
Among the names are some well-known figures,
including SpaceX and Tesla boss Elon Musk,
Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, and Zhang Yiming,
the co-founder of TikTok's parent company, ByteDance.
John Ruich, NPR News.
The USS Theodore Roosevelt has arrived in the Middle East
where the U.S. has been engaged
in more than eight months of war with Iran.
President Trump is, again, expected to discuss Iran
during his nuclear talks with the leaders of Russia
and China during his visit to Asia.
The late labor and civil rights leader Dolores Huerta
will lie in honor today at the California State Capitol
in Sacramento.
From conversation KQED, Farida Javalarumero reports.
Huerta will make history as the first non-elected person
and first woman to lie in honor at the state capitol,
where two Latinos lead the legislature
and the first elected Latino governor in modern history
prepares to take office.
Daughter Camila Chavez directs the Dolores Huerta Foundation.
The honor is very fitting to be there at the state capitol
for the work that she did to impact thousands
and millions of people, not only in the state of California,
but throughout her country.
Former President Barack Obama awarded Huerta
the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2012.
She's credited with coining the Social Justice rally
in Christ Sisa Puede, or Yes We Can.
For NPR News, I'm Farida Javalarumero in Oakland, California.
This is NPR News.
The Massachusetts mother, criminally charged
with killing her three children in 2023,
faces a new trial next spring.
Lindsay Clancy's last trial ended in a hung jury.
There had been speculation that the mistrial
might spur prosecutors to consider lesser charges
that would not require a jury,
such as manslaughter or second-degree murder,
but no changes to the charges were made
in today's court hearing.
Warren Buffett's now pledging a gift
around $5.5 billion worth of Berkshire Hathaway shares
to his family's foundations.
That would be more than four times as large
as his Thanksgiving pledges in recent years.
To maintain a healthy weight, the American public's advised
to watch what they eat and get some exercise,
but NPR's Maria Godoy reports how much we sleep
can also have a powerful impact on weight.
Adults are supposed to sleep seven to nine hours a night.
Many of us don't hit that mark.
Research has shown insufficient sleep can lead to weight gain,
primarily by driving us to eat more,
especially later in the day,
says Seth Creasy of the University of Colorado Anschutz.
If you're getting less sleep, you're eating on average.
You know, if you pull across studies,
it's around 300 calories more that you're eating per day.
Imaging studies have shown that when we're short on sleep,
activity ramps up in areas of the brain
involved in pleasure and reward,
making it harder to resist sweet and salty snacks.
But research has also linked eating fruits and vegetables
high in fiber and other nutrients
to better sleep and fewer awakenings at night.
Maria Godoy, NPR News.
This is NPR News.

Online petition with over 170,000 names urges NVIDIA to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO
USS Theodore Roosevelt arrives in Middle East amid U.S. war with Iran
Dolores Huerta to lie in honor at California State Capitol in Sacramento
Lindsay Clancy faces new trial next spring after hung jury in children's deaths
Warren Buffett pledges about $5.5 billion in Berkshire Hathaway shares to family foundations
Study links insufficient sleep to weight gain and higher evening calorie intake
